en: The Questions of King Milinda, Chapter on Investigation: 11.
The Question on the Characteristic of Volition (Cetanā)
“Venerable Nāgasena, what is the characteristic of volition?
“It has the characteristic of intending, Great King, and it has the characteristic of forming [kamma],” he replied.
“Just as, great king, some man might prepare poison and drink it himself and give it to others to drink;

he would suffer pain himself, and others too would suffer pain—in the same way, great king, here a certain person, having willed an unwholesome deed through volition, upon the breakup of the body, after death, might reappear in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, even in hell.”
Those who train according to his example also, upon the breakup of the body after death, reappear in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a lower realm, or hell.

Or again, Great King, it is as if some man were to mix together ghee, fresh butter, oil, honey, and molasses, and having prepared this, he were to drink it himself and give it to others to drink; he would be happy himself, and others would also be happy.

"In the same way, Great King, here a certain person, having willed a wholesome deed through volition, after the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in a happy destination, in a heavenly world.
And those who train in accordance with him, they too, after the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a happy destination, in a heavenly world.
Thus, Great King, volition has the characteristic of willing and the characteristic of forming."
Thus ends the eleventh question, concerning the characteristic of volition.
